CA.notes: 1%-12.3% (+1% over $1M). Up to a $20,000 exclusion of military retired pay/SBP for tax years 2025-2029 (SB 132, 2025 budget). The governor's proposal carried AGI caps (<$125k single); confirm the enacted limits.

WA.notes: No wage income tax. A 7% capital gains tax (9.9% over $1M) applies to long-term gains above about $270k.

VA.notes: 2%-5.75% (top bracket from $17k). Up to a $40,000 subtraction of military retired pay from 2025 on.

MA.notes: 5% flat, plus a 4% surtax on income over about $1.08M. US military pensions are exempt.

PA.notes: 3.07% flat with no standard deduction, plus local earned income taxes (~1-3.8%). Retirement income, including military, is exempt.

NY.notes: About 3.9%-10.9% (2026 middle-class rate cuts). NYC adds about 3-3.9% for residents. Military pensions are fully exempt.

NC.notes: 3.99% flat (2026), standard deduction $12,750. Military retired pay is exempt with 20+ years of service or a medical retirement (Bailey/2021 law). A 20-year retiree qualifies.

GA.notes: 4.99% flat for 2026 (HB 463, falling toward 3.99%), $12k standard exemption. Under 62: a $17,500 military retirement exclusion, plus another $17,500 if GA earned income exceeds $17,500. 62+: general retirement exclusion of $35k, or $65k at 65+.

CO.notes: 4.4% of federal taxable income (TABOR temporary cuts possible). Under 55: limited military retirement subtraction (verify, about $15k). 55-64: $20k pension subtraction. 65+: $24k.

OR.notes: 4.75%-9.9% (8.75% from about $11k), with a limited federal tax subtraction. Military retired pay is taxable except the portion for service before Oct 1991. Some small credits apply.

AZ.notes: 2.5% flat with the federal standard deduction. Military retired pay has been fully exempt since 2021.

TN.notes: No tax on wages; the Hall tax was repealed in 2021.

AK.notes: No personal income tax (PFD dividend paid to residents).

NH.notes: No wage tax; the interest/dividends tax was repealed from 2025.

IL.notes: 4.95% flat with a personal exemption of about $2,850. All retirement income, including military, is exempt.

_general.notes: Effective rate = state income tax / gross income for a single filer, all wage income, standard deduction, no local tax. These are model approximations (+/-0.5pp) using 2025/26 brackets. Under SCRA/MSRRA, active-duty military pay is taxable only by the state of legal residence (domicile), not the duty-station state. Military retired pay is taxed by the retiree's state of residence after retirement. Several states (e.g. CA, OR, NY, VA) do not exempt active-duty pay for their own domiciliaries, though some do.
